# hivelocity_ip_assignment_route (Resource)

Statically routes an existing IP assignment (subnet) to a next-hop IP, typically an address already configured on one of your devices. Destroying the resource clears the assignment's routing. New IP space itself is requested from Hivelocity support (or `POST /ip/`, which opens a ticket) and then looked up with the `hivelocity_ip_assignment` data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "hivelocity_ip_assignment" "subnet" {
  filter {
    name   = "subnet"
    values = ["66.165.231.128/29"]
  }
}

# Statically route the subnet to an address configured on one of your devices.
resource "hivelocity_ip_assignment_route" "subnet" {
  assignment_id = data.hivelocity_ip_assignment.subnet.assignment_id
  next_hop_ip   = "66.165.231.10"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `assignment_id` (Number) ID of the IP assignment to route.
- `next_hop_ip` (String) IPv4 or IPv6 address traffic for the assignment is routed to.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `device_id` (Number) Device currently receiving the assignment's traffic, if any.
- `facility_code` (String) Facility of the assignment.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `port_id` (Number) Port currently receiving the assignment's traffic, if any.
- `subnet` (String) CIDR of the assignment.
- `version` (Number) IP version (4 or 6).
- `vlan_id` (Number) VLAN currently receiving the assignment's traffic, if any.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the IP assignment ID
terraform import hivelocity_ip_assignment_route.subnet 4321
```
